tei:titleStmt.tei:title: שְׁנֵים עָשָׂר בָּנִים
Shném 'Asar Banim — a shiv’ata cycle for Musaf on the Shabbat of a bat mitsvah, by Isaac Gantwerk Mayer

tei:div.tei:head: Shném 'Asar Banim — a shiv’ata cycle for Musaf on the Shabbat of a bat mitsvah, by Isaac Gantwerk Mayer

tei:lg.tei:l: Twelve sons; one is the dove.
The daughters see her and call her content in cheer.
On this one’s bat mitsvah day, she has grown, for the time has come,
and she said, “My faith and law I accept like the mothers of the rose.”
Blessed are You, Cause, Shield of Abraham.
You are mighty...
Twelve tribes You made pass in the sea,
and thus Miriam sang with her brothers.
On this one’s bat mitsvah day, the merits of the commandments in their filling are
to her, living are the waters of the living and enduring Deity.
Blessed are You, Cause, who revives the dead.
Ashkenaz: Let’s exult in You... Sefarad: A crown...
Twelve zodiac signs; their ring is in their firmament.
Israel hears the voice of the Deity (on Shabbat Shuvah: Sovereign), exalted and thundering.
On this one’s bat mitsvah day, the crowns of Your holy Torah grant her, because
all its teachings are good, and its paths are pleasant paths.
Blessed are You, Cause, the holy Deity (on Shabbat Shuvah: Sovereign)
You established...
Twelve months from Nisan to Adar,
their first-day given to women in splendor and splendiferousness
On this one’s bat mitsvah day, make her rejoice on the delineated day
that has pleasures deriving from the Awesome in Holiness!
Blessed are You, Cause, who sanctifies the sabbath.
Desire...
Twelve pillars facing the Mount of Glory
were brought together by the watcher to serve as a reminder.
On this one’s bat mitsvah day, her father calls, and her mother says,
“You may say: ‘my desire is to keep the watch.’”
Blessed are You, Cause, who returns Their presence to Ẓíōn.
We thank...
Twelve stones of onyx, stones to be set,
the names of the tribes and the donations of the princes.
On this one’s bat mitsvah day she will thank thanks to the Wonderworker:
“To me You have contributed! Thus Your goodness we call.”
Blessed are You, Cause, whose name is good, to You it is pleasing to praise.
Grant...
Twelve years Ẓíōn’s daughter celebrates her advancement.
She is worthy of the Deity, who gives her fulfillment.
On this one’s bat mitsvah day, be strong! Be courageous! And say before the nation,
“I will do the commandments of the Awesome One, as I become a young woman.”
Blessed are You, Cause, who blesses Their people Israel in peace.

tei:note.tei:p: A dual meaning, referring to Song of Songs 6:9 (as does the next verse) but also to the fact that Jacob had twelve sons and one daughter.
The opening word of the last line of each stanza comes from Ruth 3:6
Referring to the matriarchs. “The rose” is a poetic term for Israel.
On the day the Torah was given, the angels gave Israel two crowns.
Find Proverbs 4:2 and 3:17, recited at the end of the Torah service.

Rosh Ḥodesh, the new moon, has long been in many mystical circles a holiday of women. The original reasoning for this was probably biological, but many other spiritual explanations have been suggested over the years.
Though often mistranslated in Christian circles, the word almah has no connotations of sexual status whatsoever in Hebrew, referring to any young unmarried adult woman.
